title: How I vibecoded a GTA-inspired third-person shooter
author: IVibedAlot
selftext:
Hey everyone!

A little background about me: I've been a game developer for around 15 years. I spent about 6 years working in mobile games, and most of the rest of my career has been focused on PC games with my small studio. These days, though, I'm working as a solo dev.

# About the project

This is a mission-based third-person shooter, with 2D visual novel sections between missions using a semi-realistic art style.

The game is being developed in Unity 6.3.

# AI stack

The project originally started with **Codex Pro 5X**, and I also experimented with the **Astra** model for a few days. It didn't work as well as I hoped for this particular project, so I eventually switched development over to **Claude Code with Opus 5.5**, usually running at High effort or above depending on the session.

**ChatGPT** handles a lot of the planning, resource creation, concept work, and helps me prepare/refine prompts.

Some other AI tools/platforms involved:

* **WriteWithPaige** — writing and mission design
* **Nano-GPT** — access to different models depending on the task, including Seedream, Wan, etc.
* **Tripo 3D** — character model generation and rigging

# What you're seeing in the clip

**Shooter framework:**  
The core TPS system comes from an Asset Store package, but I've vibecoded quite a lot on top of it to fit the game. This includes changes and improvements to audio, animations, gameplay logic, enemy behavior, and the overall shooting experience.

**Characters:**  
For the main character, ChatGPT generated the original concept art, Seedream was used for several revisions to get the design closer to what I wanted, and Tripo 3D was used to generate the 3D model and rig it.

The enemies and most of their animations come from Asset Store assets and ActorCore.

**Environment:**  
The original environment assets also come from the Asset Store, but the final maps have been heavily modified through shaders, lighting, materials, and scene setup.

The interesting part is that I built the map entirely through prompts with Opus. I didn't manually place or edit things inside the Unity editor.

The map layout itself is based on the story and mission design that had already been created by the AI handling the writing side of the project.

**UI:**  
All of the UI was designed/generated with ChatGPT and then implemented in Unity through Claude Code.

**Music & Sound:**  
Most of the music and sound effects were purchased from the Unity Asset Store and AudioStock.

# The overall experiment

For this project, I've basically been working entirely through prompts.

I don't manually edit things inside the engine, and I don't write the game code myself. My role is closer to directing the project: defining what I want, reviewing the result, testing it, identifying problems, and iterating through prompts until it works the way I want.

At this point, the game's core systems/framework are basically complete, along with **Chapter 1**. The mission shown in the clip is the Chapter 1 mission.

The next stage is mostly mass production: building out the remaining missions, chapters, environments, and content using the framework that's already in place.

I’m keeping this post focused purely on the development process, so I’m not including any store links here.

Thanks for reading, and good luck with your own vibe coding projects!
